newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Low inflation threatens Brazil's Treasury accounts.
newsitem.headline: Low inflation threatens Brazil's Treasury accounts.

text.p: Low inflation may deepen the imbalance in Brazil's Treasury accounts and in part jeopardize efforts to reduce the fiscal deficit this year, financial newspaper Gazeta Mercantil said on Thursday.
August inflation at 0.004 percent as measured by the IGP-M index has raised real interest rates on internal debt to 1.67 percent last month from 0.68 percent in July, the newspaper said.
If monthly inflation was maintained at 0.5 percent, as the government expects, the impact of the real interest rates on expenses would persist, Gazeta said.

On Wednesday, Treasury secretary Murilo Portugal announced a primary surplus of 201 million reais and an operational deficit of 1.366 billion reais for August. The deficit was due to expenses with payment of interest rates.
The primary result is the operational balance excluding interest payments.
